thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] (customer) and [COMPANY] (Bluetooth SIG certification consultant) work through a multi-month registration update for two automotive Bluetooth products, HM23 and HM26, following a change to the Host Subsystem and Profile Subsystem QDIDs driven by an Android OS update. The thread covers whether a third-party (different company's) test report can be reused for the registration update, the discovery of a missing mandatory RF PHY test item in that report (apparently a BQTF/test-lab oversight), and the chipset vendor's creation of Subset DNs to remove no-longer-supported features (Power Class 1 for HM26, AoA/AoD for HM23) so existing test evidence can still be reused. The consultant ultimately resolves the missing-test-item problem without requiring new testing, by using a post-July-2024 registration-site capability to combine an already-approved QDID's RF/RF PHY layers with a vendor Subset DN's other layers. The thread closes with the consultant providing, and then correcting, step-by-step self-service instructions so the customer can perform a similar DN-combination registration without commissioning full agency service.
all_questions_found: Can the consultant's SIG registration support service use a different company's existing test report when updating an End Product registration after the Host Subsystem and Profile Subsystem QDIDs change due to an Android OS update?
Will a third-party RF/RF PHY test report submitted for the product remain valid/usable as-is after the upcoming TCRL2024-1 test-item effective date (2024-12-28)?

Does a missing mandatory RF PHY test item in the submitted report (required since TCRL2022-1, apparently a testing-lab oversight) need to be resolved before the report can be reused to update the Host/Profile subsystem registration that Includes the existing, already-approved Controller Subsystem QDID?
Can the missing RF PHY test item be performed as a stand-alone delta/differential test?

If the missing RF PHY test item is performed as a delta test and reflected into the new registration, does that count as an ICS change that would trigger a full RF PHY test requirement and inter-layer Consistency Check exposure?
What would it cost to add only the single missing RF PHY test item?

Does the chipset vendor's new Subset DN that removes Power Class 1 support resolve the previously flagged inter-layer consistency concern, and can the existing RF/RF PHY test report still be used as registration evidence under that Subset DN?
After the chipset vendor completes removal of AoA/AoD support, is the previously proposed test-report-reuse registration approach now confirmed workable?
Is there a way the customer can perform a DN-combination (Include) registration covering specific subsystems themselves, without commissioning the consultant's full registration-agency service?
What are the exact Layer Selection / ICS Selection / Consistency Check / Test Coverage Waiver steps needed to complete that self-service combination registration?
(Correction) Which Core-layer ICS item should actually be unchecked in the self-service procedure -- ICS 10/1 or ICS 12/1?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread works through how an already-approved QDID's test evidence interacts with a later registration update: Including an approved QDID without touching its ICS does not resurface gaps in its underlying test report, but reusing that same report as fresh evidence for a new registration does expose the gap. It covers inter-layer Consistency Check mechanics (touching and reverting an RF PHY ICS item still triggers a consistency evaluation against updated Host/Profile layers, which can surface unrelated shortfalls such as SCPP), Test Coverage Waiver (TCW) usage, and the post-July-2024 registration site's ability to build a registration by combining layers from two different existing DNs/QDIDs (one for RF/RF PHY, another for the remaining layers) rather than treating the report as monolithic new evidence.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: The deciding principle is that an already-SIG-approved QDID's formal status is fixed: as long as it is Included unmodified, any quality gap in the test evidence behind it does not get re-examined. A gap only becomes a live problem when the same report is resubmitted as evidence for a brand-new registration. Given that, the correct move is not to retest or to risk an ICS edit-and-revert (which exposes the registration to a full inter-layer Consistency Check), but to keep the valid RF/RF PHY layers anchored to the original approved QDID via a combination (Include) registration with the vendor's Subset DN supplying the remaining layers -- carrying forward the originally-valid evidence intact.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Reusing a flawed report as fresh evidence for a new registration would expose the missing RF PHY test item as a live deficiency. Deliberately editing and reverting the RF PHY ICS to add the missing item risks triggering inter-layer Consistency Check failures against the updated Host/Profile subsystem content (e.g., if the updated Host subsystem supports Isochronous mode or AoA/AoD), which the thread illustrates with an SCPP shortfall example. Paying for unnecessary retesting was also a live risk: no price existed for a single missing item, and a 2-item test was quoted at ¥200,000, though the thread notes the customer has a basis to request the missing item be retested free of charge by the original testing lab since the gap was its oversight.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: In the step-by-step self-service registration instructions, the consultant told the customer to uncheck Core-layer ICS item 10/1, then corrected this in the next message to say it was a typo and the correct item is ICS 12/1, with 10/1 actually needing to remain checked. Future instructions involving specific ICS item numbers should be double-checked before sending, since a single transposed digit changes which subsystem capability gets excluded from the registration.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a piece of test evidence has a verified gap relative to current requirements, the first question should not be 'how do we retest' but 'does the registration mechanics let us carry forward the existing approved evidence untouched.' Combination (Include) registrations that pair an already-approved QDID's valid layers with a vendor Subset DN's remaining layers can legitimately avoid retriggering a known evidence gap, and this option should be checked before quoting retest costs or accepting Consistency Check risk from an ICS edit-and-revert.
